_comment: Schema contract - what import_to_egdb.py builds in the Enterprise Geodatabase.
Generated by analyze_source.py from the source named below; safe to edit by hand,
which is the point: every field carries the measurement its type was chosen from,
so disagreeing with the inference does not mean re-reading the data.
Types are ArcGIS field types, not PostgreSQL ones. An Enterprise Geodatabase has
no boolean type, so a boolean column appears here as SHORT with the substitution
recorded in its evidence block rather than applied silently.

generated.types_from: the source's own fields block, with the measurement recorded beside it

spatial_reference.decided_by: spatialReference.latestWkid=3857, wkid=102100 in the source file
spatial_reference.note: A feature class holds exactly one spatial reference, and creating it with the wrong one does not error at write time - the coordinates are simply interpreted as the wrong grid. Only a bounding-box check notices.

geometry.note: x_column feeds the easting/longitude and y_column the northing/latitude. The contract names them separately rather than as a pair so that an axis swap is a visible edit rather than an ordering assumption.

name_limits.note: Enterprise geodatabase limits, tighter than PostgreSQL's own 63 characters. ArcGIS does not delimit object names, so a name that would need quoting - mixed case, a space, a reserved word - is a name ArcGIS cannot address even though PostgreSQL stores it.
